common_name: Blaze Winter Pea (High-Yielding Cold-Hardy Forage Pea)

planting.note: Drill or broadcast inoculated seed in fall through early winter; Blaze's cold tolerance lets it hold up through colder winters than many older Austrian winter pea strains.

directions: Blaze is a white-flowered, yellow-seeded winter pea bred by ProGene Plant Research and marketed for both cold-climate dryland grain trials and fall cover cropping, combining strong winter hardiness with solid biomass and nitrogen-fixing capacity. Seed into a well-drained, fall seedbed from early September through December in regions with mild winters, using fresh legume inoculant for best nodulation. The sprawling vines benefit from being mixed with a cereal grain such as rye or oats for structural support and weed suppression through winter. Terminate by mowing, rolling, or incorporating in spring near flowering to maximize the nitrogen contribution to the following cash crop.

common_name: Sugar Graze Ultra Sorghum-Sudangrass (Photoperiod-Sensitive Grazing Hybrid)
scientific_name: Sorghum bicolor × Sorghum bicolor var. sudanense 'Sugar Graze Ultra'

planting.note: Drill or broadcast after soil has warmed well past 65°F, typically a few weeks after the last frost through early June; photoperiod sensitivity delays flowering until after the summer solstice.

directions: Sugar Graze Ultra is a photoperiod-sensitive sorghum-sudangrass hybrid that stays vegetative through the long days of summer rather than racing to head out, extending the window for rotational grazing or repeated cutting before seed set. Delayed flowering also reduces the management headaches of coordinating grazing around heading and keeps forage quality higher later into the season than day-neutral sorghum-sudan types. Drill into warm soil after frost danger has passed, and graze or mow once the stand reaches a safe height to avoid prussic acid risk in new regrowth. Allow adequate regrowth between grazings and terminate by mowing, grazing down, or winter-kill before fall planting.
